mechanism: The reanchored thick parent is enclosed in the centered (8A)-homothety of a thin tube with the same new axis/base and radius rho. This intermediate thin carrier need not coincide with the original parent carrier.

Equal-volume unit tubes at a common radius and homothety volume scaling then give volume(new) <= (8A)^3 volume(oldParent), even for a different old parent at radius rho. This is an upper bound, not an exact Jacobian for thickening a fixed-length tube.
The raw volume bound needs rho>=0 and A>=1, with arbitrary center, no small-scale or axial-shift hypothesis. Those geometric restrictions enter other containment uses.

The general coaxial helper separately requires equal oriented directions, base displacement shift, positive inner/outer factors, radial inequality inner*r_source<=outer*r_target and axial inequality abs(shift)+inner/2<=outer/2. Its explicit inverse homothety verifies both segment parameter and transverse distance.

Doubled reanchored parent containment in the original 32A-dilation additionally assumes abs(axialShift)<=4A. The active-parent wrapper derives this from positive delta/rho, delta<=1,rho<=1,radius<=1/4,A>=1, common point and FULL source-carrier containment.
limits: Imported closest-point, tube-volume equality, homothety-volume and active-parent axial-shift arguments are dependencies, not newly fully audited here.
No deletion of the volume overhead, no global scale-free transport, no full John-rescaling audit, no upstream Kakeya theorem certification, new theorem, score or paper.
hypothesis: A scale contract for common-anchor regrouping must retain an explicit finite volume overhead and the distinct provenance/containment conditions; equal tube radius alone does not identify carriers.
falsifier: A claimed sharp identity volume(new)=(8A)^3 volume(old), or original-parent doubled-containment without an axial displacement restriction, would require a new argument; the present source asserts neither.
